site.markdown_nice_read_plain: Markdown, nice to read and plain to edit.
site.md_reader_shows_markdown: md-reader shows Markdown with its real formatting and lets you edit the text as it is. Reader, editor, or both at once, in light or dark mode.
site.free_no_ads_one: Free, no ads. One click: it brings everything it needs, you don't need Python installed. Windows 10 or 11.
site.this_is_live_demo: This is a live demo: write in the left panel and the right one changes as you type. The program does the same, with your own files.
site.no_word_processor_in: No word processor in between: the file stays plain Markdown, and you see it formatted while you work on it.
site.headings_bold_italics_strikethrough: Headings, bold, italics, strikethrough, nested lists, task boxes, tables, code, quotes, rules, links and images. Links to a section (#…) or to another .md open inside the program.
site.reader_editor_markdown_text: Reader, Editor (the Markdown text as it is, with a subtle highlight) and Dual (both at once: what you type shows up right away). Ctrl+E switches between reader and editor in the same window.
site.click_task_box_tick: Click a task box to tick it (it changes [ ] ↔ [x] in the text), and Ctrl+E opens the editor right where you clicked.
site.select_piece_right_click: Select a piece and right click: bold, italics, strikethrough, code, link, headings, lists, task boxes, quote or code block, in the editor or in the reader. F1 opens a guide with every format, how to write it and how it looks.
site.ctrl_c_in_reader: Ctrl+C in the reader copies with formatting: paste into Word, Writer or an email and the headings, bold, lists and tables stay. Or More ▸ “Copy all with formatting” for the whole document.
site.one_button_or_follow: One button, or follow the system setting. The same simple look as cam-ui.
site.side_outline_with_document: A side outline with the document's headings, search with Ctrl+F, zoom with Ctrl+= and Ctrl+-, and recent files.
site.saves_in_same_format: It saves in the same format it opened them: encoding, BOM and Windows line endings. If the file changes outside the program it reloads by itself; if you have unsaved changes, it warns you instead of overwriting them.
site.checks_for_new_version: It checks for a new version when it opens and asks first (or not, if you prefer). It keeps a copy of the previous version so you can go back with one click.
site.reader_dark_mode_document: Reader, dark mode. The document with its formatting and the outline of headings on the side.
site.light_mode_one_button: Light mode. One button switches it, or it follows the system.
site.dual_text_on_left: Dual. The text on the left, the result on the right, updated as you type.
site.one_small_file_md: One small file, md-reader-instalar-en.cmd. You can read it before running it.
site.if_windows_warns_you: If Windows warns you, choose “More info” and “Run anyway”. It sets up its own Python (you don't need one) and takes a minute or two the first time.
site.use_from_start_menu: Use it from the Start menu
site.md_reader_opens_when: md-reader opens when it finishes, and appears in the Explorer's “Open with” for .md files. To always open them with it: right click on one ▸ Open with ▸ Choose another app ▸ md-reader ▸ “Always”.
site.open_with_right_click: Open it with right click ▸ Open
site.first_time_macos_asks: The first time, macOS asks for confirmation because it is not from the App Store. A terminal window shows the progress.
site.ends_up_in_applications: It ends up in the Applications folder of your user (~/Applications), opens when it finishes, and appears in “Open with” for .md files.
site.with_python_3_10: With Python 3.10 or newer (on Linux, the system one with python3-tk):
site.what_does_installer_put: What does the installer put on my computer?
site.everything_goes_into_your: Everything goes into your own user folders: on Windows the program in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\md-reader and its own Python in %LOCALAPPDATA%\md-reader, with a Start menu and desktop shortcut, and it appears in “Installed apps”; on macOS, md-reader.app in ~/Applications. It does not touch any Python you already have, or ask for administrator rights.
site.on_windows_from_settings: On Windows, from Settings → Apps → Installed apps, “md-reader”. On macOS, run the uninstaller the installer tells you about at the end (bash “~/Library/Application Support/md-reader/uninstall.sh”). Your Markdown files are never touched.
site.why_does_windows_warn: Why does Windows warn me about the file?
site.installer_is_plain_script: The installer is a plain script that is not signed by a company, and Windows warns about any downloaded script. Open it with a text editor if you want to check it: it only downloads md-reader, its Python and its two libraries.
site.not_yet_with_installer: Not yet with the installer: the Python it would bring on Linux draws text with old, unsmoothed fonts, and it would look bad. From the source code with the system's Python (python3-tk package) it works fine.
site.no_only_connects_this: No. It only connects to this page to check for updates. Your documents stay on your computer.
site.yes_checks_for_newer: Yes. It checks for a newer version when it opens and asks before installing it; you can also check by hand in More ▸ “Check for updates”, or tick “update automatically when opening”. It keeps a copy of the version you had and can go back to it with one click.
site.is_worth_writing_even: It is worth writing even if everything worked: it tells me what to look after.
site.what_you_use_for: What you use it for, what you liked and what cost you.
site.file_looks_wrong_something: A file looks wrong, something is not saved, the program closes.
site.tell_me_what_you: Tell me what you are trying to do and I will look at how to make it possible.
site.you_need_free_github: You need a free GitHub account. You can also read what others have sent.
site.md_reader_is_free: md-reader is free and has no ads. If it is useful to you, buy me a coffee and help me keep improving it.
site.is_also_inside_program: It is also inside the program: More ▸ “About md-reader”, with a little demo of the dual mode that types itself. Made with care by Jaime Luis Olguín Mesina.
site.alt_md_reader_in: md-reader in dark mode, as a reader, with the outline on the left
site.alt_md_reader_in_3: md-reader in dual mode: Markdown text on the left and the result on the right
site.alt_md_reader_about: md-reader “About” window, with a demo that types itself and the Ko-fi button
site.demo_label: md-reader demo: type on the left and see it on the right
site.js.note_mac: Free, no ads. Unzip it and open the installer with right click ▸ Open. macOS 11 or newer.
site.js.note_linux: There is no Linux installer yet (see “And Linux?” below); it works from the source code.
